svg.text: The lecturer's 11-step ECG comment, with the numbers to check

g.text: 1. Identification
Name, age, date/time, clinical context
2. Standardisation
Calibration box 10 mm = 1 mV (2 big squares) · 25 mm/s
3. Voltage
High: (S V1 or V2) + (R V5 or V6) ≥ 35 mm → LVH
Low*: QRS < 5 mm in all limb leads (< 10 mm chest)
4. Axis
Normal −30° to +90° · LAD −30 to −90 · RAD +90 to +180
Quick: lead I + lead II both upright = normal
5. Rhythm
Regular vs irregular: compare R–R with calipers/paper
6. Rate
Regular: 300 ÷ big squares, or 1500 ÷ small squares (R–R)
Irregular: QRS in 6 s (30 big squares) × 10
7. P wave
Upright I & II, inverted aVR · height ≤ 2.5 mm · width ≤ 0.10 s
Tall (> 2.5 mm) = P pulmonale (RA) · wide/notched = P mitrale (LA)
Absent: AF, flutter, junctional, SVT
8. PR interval
0.12–0.20 s (3–5 small squares)
Long → AV block · Short → pre-excitation (WPW), junctional
9. QRS
Normal ≤ 0.08–0.10 s · ≥ 0.12 s = bundle branch block / ventricular
RBBB: rSR′ "M" in V1, wide S in V6 · LBBB: deep QS V1, "M" V6
Pathological Q: > 1 small sq wide or > ¼ R height
10. ST segment
Iso-electric · ↑ in ≥ 2 contiguous leads = STEMI (territory)
↓ = ischaemia / reciprocal / NSTEMI · diffuse ↑ + PR↓ = pericarditis
11. T wave
Normally inverted aVR (± V1, III) · peaked = ↑K⁺ · deep ↓ = ischaemia
STEMI territory map (leads → artery)
Inferior II, III, aVF → RCA (reciprocal I, aVL) · add V4R for RV infarct
Septal V1–V2 · Anterior V3–V4 → LAD · Lateral I, aVL, V5–V6 → LCx/diagonal
Posterior ST↓ + tall R in V1–V3 → confirm ST↑ in V7–V9 · Extensive anterior V1–V6 + I, aVL → proximal LAD
Paper: 1 small square = 1 mm = 0.04 s = 0.1 mV · 1 big square = 5 mm = 0.20 s · 5 big squares = 1 s · 300 big = 1 min
* low-voltage cut-offs and the territory map are added (slides give only the headings); everything else is from the slides.
